idiom_name: runtime_checkable Protocol + isinstance; hasattr / collections.abc structural checks
implementation_notes: Declare the client-specific contract as a typing.Protocol and ask with isinstance once it is decorated @runtime_checkable: the check is structural (every protocol member must exist on the object; properties are no longer evaluated as of 3.12), which is exactly 'does this component support interface X' made checkable without the component inheriting from anything. collections.abc has performed the same structural probe for years (isinstance(x, Iterable/Iterator/Sized)), and the typing documentation recommends plain hasattr when a full protocol check is too slow. Supplying an extension for a foreign object is a per-instance attribute, a wrapper class or a __getattr__-delegating adapter - the roles stay the same, but a delegating adapter must implement __dir__ and be careful that __getattr__ does not answer every name.
pitfalls: @runtime_checkable verifies only that members exist, not their signatures or types: a wrong signature passes the probe and fails at call time.
Protocol isinstance can evaluate properties and __getattr__ (before 3.12), triggering side effects during a 'harmless' check; since 3.12 instance attributes must exist statically.
An object whose __getattr__ returns something for every name satisfies every runtime-checkable protocol, making the probe meaningless.
Structural protocol checks are noticeably slower than hasattr - probe once and cache the decision instead of testing in hot paths.
